buttonLabel: "Explore Costa Rica's mountains and beaches"
lead: >-
  This nine-day Costa Rica journey starts in Liberia and travels through the volcanic region of Rincón de la Vieja, Río Celeste, Arenal and the Monteverde cloud forests. Activities include ziplining, tubing, horse riding, an introduction to Maleku culture and crossing Lake Arenal by Taxi–Boat–Taxi. The final days are spent on the northern Pacific coast.
---

## Costa Rica: beaches and mountains in 9 days

This tour is designed for travellers who want to **take part in outdoor activities themselves**, rather than simply observe natural attractions from viewpoints. The itinerary includes ziplining, canyon rappelling, river tubing, horse riding and forest trails. After several activity-filled days, it reaches the [Pacific coast](/costa-rica/place/pacific-coast/), where there is free time.

The programme lasts **9 days and 8 nights**, beginning and ending in [Liberia](/costa-rica/place/liberia/). This is a significant difference from many tours starting and finishing in San José. When booking flights, pay attention to Daniel Oduber Airport in Liberia and your return transfer route.

## Rincón de la Vieja: the most active day

After arrival, you head towards [Rincón de la Vieja](/costa-rica/place/rincon-de-la-vieja/). Day two features four activities: ziplining, rappelling in Río Blanco canyon, tubing on the Río Negro through **Class II rapids**, and horseback riding. Afterwards, you can relax in volcanic hot springs, steam baths and mud baths.

Tubing has restrictions: **participants must be at least 8 years old and 140 cm tall**. This is particularly relevant for families; travelling with an adult does not override the participation requirements. A guide provides safety instructions before the activities, and individual medical or physical limitations must be assessed separately.

The region is known for volcanic phenomena and varied scenery. Nevertheless, a hike to the active Rincón de la Vieja crater should not be assumed to be included merely because the tour passes nearby. The specified activities focus on the canyon, river, horse riding and thermal springs.

## Río Celeste and Tenorio National Park

On day three, the route heads for [Tenorio Volcano National Park](/costa-rica/place/tenorio-volcano-national-park/) and the [Río Celeste](/costa-rica/place/rio-celeste/). The main walk crosses humid tropical forest to sections of the striking blue river. Special attention is paid to Los Teñideros, where the meeting of watercourses is associated with the river's distinctive colour.

Forest-trail footwear and rain protection are essential. Water colour, access to different sections and walking conditions all depend on the weather. Leave room in your luggage for wet clothing and do not treat dramatic photographs of the river as a promise that it will always look the same.

After Tenorio, the itinerary explores northern Costa Rica and continues to the Arenal area, linking volcanic scenery with humid forest ecosystems.

## Meeting the Maleku people and relaxing in hot springs

A separate day is dedicated to **Palenque Tonjibe** village. Here, visitors learn about the contemporary traditions of the Indigenous Maleku people: crafts, homes, uses of plants and local culture. A forest walk introduces plants historically used by the region's inhabitants.

This offers something different from an entirely nature-focused excursion. Treat the village visit as an encounter with people and their traditions, respect local photography rules and protect residents' privacy.

Later, the journey continues to [La Fortuna and Arenal Volcano](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/) for relaxation in hot springs, a change of pace after walking and transfers.

## Arenal, Mistico and traces of an earlier eruption

Day five takes place near Arenal. The route includes Mistico hanging bridges, where trails pass through different levels of tropical forest, and Arenal Volcano 1968 park. The latter is named after the volcano's famous eruption; sections of old lava material can still be seen in the landscape.

The Mistico complex has **15 bridges, including 6 hanging bridges**, and its trails take approximately 2.5 hours. The effort here is different from canyon rappelling and tubing: the focus is on walking forest paths and bridges. Humidity, uneven ground and weather still matter.

On such excursions, expect an experience of the natural environment rather than a guaranteed encounter with a particular animal. Birds and monkeys may appear along the route, but wild animals do not keep to a timetable.

## Arenal to Monteverde: Taxi–Boat–Taxi

On day six, the journey continues to [Monteverde and Santa Elena](/costa-rica/place/monteverde-santa-elena/). The programme specifies a **Taxi–Boat–Taxi** transfer: a vehicle to Lake Arenal, a boat across the lake and another vehicle to Monteverde. This is the actual transport sequence, relevant when planning luggage and preparing for the weather.

Monteverde is known for cloud forests, a cool humid climate and vegetation different from the Arenal area. The itinerary mentions Selvatura Zip Lines and hanging bridges. The exact set of paid activities should be checked against the confirmed programme when needed: mentioning a park does not automatically mean every activity there is included.

This stage is especially rewarding for travellers who want to compare lowland tropical forest, volcanic country and cloud forest in a single trip.

## The Pacific coast finale

After Monteverde, there is a transfer to the northern [Pacific coast](/costa-rica/place/pacific-coast/). Day eight is entirely free for seaside relaxation or independently arranged optional activities. Day nine includes breakfast and a transfer to Liberia Airport.

Compared with the [seven-day tour featuring Tamarindo Beach](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-short-complete-tour/), this option has a longer, more varied active section and fewer free beach days. In return, it offers a dedicated adventure day, Maleku cultural experiences and the Lake Arenal crossing.

## Included services and who the tour suits

The price includes accommodation, local taxes, excursions, transfers, entrance tickets and breakfasts, lunches and dinners on the relevant itinerary days. Optional activities, airport fees and additional hotel services cost extra. The overall list of included services **does not specify a particular guiding language**, so check this before selecting the tour.

The journey suits adults and families with older children, provided all participants meet each activity's requirements. Ziplining, canyon rappelling and tubing demand an individual assessment of physical readiness. For a more leisurely journey with nature walks and two free beach days, consider the [seven-day itinerary](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-short-complete-tour/); for Caribbean nature, see the [five-day Tortuguero trip](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-5-days/).

## Frequently asked questions about Costa Rica's mountains and beaches

### How long is the tour, and which airport does it use?

**9 days and 8 nights.** The itinerary begins and ends at Daniel Oduber Airport in Liberia.

### Can a 7-year-old take part in tubing?

No. Tubing requires a **minimum age of 8** and a **height of at least 140 cm**. Both requirements must be checked before booking.

### Does the tour include climbing to Rincón de la Vieja's crater?

No such ascent is included. The adventure day covers ziplining, canyon rappelling, tubing, horse riding and thermal springs. Access to volcanic areas is regulated separately.

### What does Taxi–Boat–Taxi mean?

It is a vehicle transfer, followed by a boat crossing of Lake Arenal and a second road journey to Monteverde. This transfer is part of day six.

### How many beach days are there?

There is free time on arrival at the northern Pacific coast, and **day 8 is entirely free**. Day 9 is departure to Liberia Airport.

## Essential Costa Rica in 5 days: why visit Tortuguero?

**This short itinerary is chosen for the nature of the Caribbean coast, waterways and early-morning rainforest excursions.** It lasts 5 days and 4 nights. The journey begins and ends in [San José](/costa-rica/place/san-jose/), with its main stop in [Tortuguero](/costa-rica/place/tortuguero/).

It suits first-time visitors to Costa Rica's natural areas who are willing to rise early to look for wildlife. Rather than trying to see all the country's national parks, it focuses on canals, forests, one coffee estate and waterfalls.

For an additional volcano and hanging bridges on the same journey, compare the [six-day Costa Rica for Nature Lovers tour](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-for-nature-lovers/). The [10-day Costa Rica Pearls itinerary](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-pearls-10-days/) suits travellers planning a much longer journey to the Pacific coast.

## What makes Tortuguero the highlight?

[Tortuguero National Park](/costa-rica/place/tortuguero/) is known for its network of canals and humid Caribbean forests. Birds, reptiles and other tropical creatures can be observed from the water. Costa Rica's official conservation authority notes the variety of waterways in the area, where boats provide access to settlements near the park.

On day two, you leave San José early, travelling through [Braulio Carrillo](/costa-rica/place/braulio-carrillo-national-park/). The road section then gives way to a boat transfer. In Tortuguero, the programme introduces the village and Caribbean scenery, followed by a sunrise boat tour of the canals the next day.

**The sunrise excursion is a chance to observe the forest coming to life, not a guarantee of any particular animal sighting.** Results depend on weather, water levels, animal behaviour and the boat's route. Pack lightweight clothing, a rain jacket, insect protection and a way to keep your equipment dry.

Do not confuse a nature-focused boat excursion with a guaranteed chance to watch sea turtles lay their eggs. This programme does not promise a separate nighttime nesting tour.

## How the five days are arranged

| Stage | Planned activities |
|---|---|
| Day 1 | Arrival in San José |
| Days 2–3 | Transfer and Tortuguero canals |
| Day 4 | Doka and La Paz waterfalls |
| Day 5 | Airport transfer |

Day four includes a **flight from Tortuguero to San José**, followed by sightseeing in the central part of the country. At [Doka Estate](/costa-rica/place/doka-estate/), you learn about coffee production, then walk among waterfalls and green hills at [La Paz Waterfall Gardens](/costa-rica/place/la-paz-waterfalls/).

This means that one day combines several places and a flight. If you want more time at the waterfalls or dedicated days in the highlands, the five-day option may feel too compressed.

## Who will enjoy this duration?

Five days allow you to experience one major natural destination and several stops near the capital. Arrival and departure days shorten the actual sightseeing time, and the itinerary involves early starts.

This is a particularly good choice when your main wish is to **see Tortuguero and add coffee and waterfalls afterwards**. For extended volcanic hikes or several nights on Pacific beaches, choose a different itinerary.

Scientific and conservation sources describe Tortuguero as a very wet region. A waterproof bag, comfortable shoes and rain protection are more practical than relying on an entirely dry spell during a particular month.

## What is included and what costs extra?

The price covers transfers, accommodation, English-language excursions, the domestic **Tortuguero–San José flight**, meals on the specified days and entrance tickets to visited attractions, except for admission to Tortuguero National Park.

That ticket costs **$17 per person** and is paid for separately. Additional activities, airport fees and personal expenses at hotels are also excluded. Distinguish the tour price from all payments made during the journey; check the park's current rules and ticket price again before visiting.

Guiding is provided in English. If you specifically need a Russian-speaking guide, do not assume this is part of the standard package.

## Frequently asked questions about the five-day Costa Rica tour

### Can we see wildlife in Tortuguero?

The programme includes boat trips along canals inhabited by birds, reptiles and other animals. You may observe them in their natural environment, but no particular species or number of sightings is guaranteed.

### Does this tour include Arenal Volcano?

No. It includes Tortuguero, Doka coffee estate and La Paz. For a visit to the [Arenal Volcano area](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/), consider the [six-day nature route](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-for-nature-lovers/).

### Is the flight from Tortuguero included?

Yes, the Tortuguero–San José flight is listed among the included services.

### Are all entrance tickets included?

No. Admission to Tortuguero National Park is paid for separately. Other tickets are covered according to the specific programme conditions.

  Extreme Costa Rica is a 13-day programme combining kayaking in Tortuguero, rafting on the Pacuare River, canyoning and quad biking near Arenal, active adventures in Monteverde and marine activities on the Pacific coast. Learn which days require physical preparation, how the stages differ, what costs extra and what to check before diving.
---

## Extreme Costa Rica: who will enjoy this 13-day journey?

**This tour is designed for travellers who want to take part in adventures rather than merely photograph volcanoes and jungles.** Over 13 days and 12 nights, the itinerary travels from [San José](/costa-rica/place/san-jose/) to the Caribbean canals of [Tortuguero](/costa-rica/place/tortuguero/), then to the [Pacuare River](/costa-rica/place/pacuare-river/), [Arenal](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/) and [Monteverde](/costa-rica/place/monteverde-santa-elena/). The final stage reaches the Pacific Ocean, with fishing near [Flamingo](/costa-rica/place/flamingo/) and diving around the [Catalina Islands](/costa-rica/place/catalina-islands/).

There are several kinds of physical demands. Kayaking on the canals requires stamina on the water; rafting involves teamwork and following the instructor's commands; canyoning requires confidence at heights and with safety harnesses. Later come ocean fishing and scuba diving, which requires a certain level of experience. It would be a mistake to treat every activity as equally easy.

For a first visit with gentler activities, compare the [short Costa Rica in 5 Days itinerary](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-essentials/) and the complete [Costa Rica tours catalogue](/costa-rica/tour/). You can find more about the country's climates and regions in the [Costa Rica guide](/costa-rica/).

## Why Tortuguero and Pacuare provide different water experiences

In [Tortuguero](/costa-rica/place/tortuguero/), the main experience is moving quietly through narrow waterways amid humid Caribbean forest. On day 2, the road ends at a pier and the journey continues by boat. On day 3, guided kayaking is scheduled. Observing birds and animals along the banks is easier from the water, but encounters with specific species cannot be guaranteed. Seeing sea turtles ashore depends on their natural cycle; the programme does not promise a separate nighttime egg-laying excursion.

The [Pacuare River](/costa-rica/place/pacuare-river/) is different: white water, rapids and active paddling rather than a leisurely wildlife trip with a camera. On the first rafting day, the group covers **13 km and 14 Class III rapids**, then stays at a riverside camp. The next day allows time for rest and activities on site. On day 6, you tackle **23 km and about 30 rapids, including Class IV**. Activity is therefore spread over several days, with changing difficulty.

This matters when selecting the tour: an appealing rafting description is no substitute for checking your skills, water conditions and the rafting operator's requirements. Share your experience and health restrictions in advance and confirm which sections are suitable for each group member. A river camp is different from a city hotel, so be prepared for the practical conditions of staying in the forest.

## Arenal and Monteverde: rappelling, speed and heights

After Pacuare, you travel to [La Fortuna and Arenal Volcano](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/). Day 7 includes canyoning in Lost Canyon: a practice descent, taller waterfalls and rope-assisted rappelling. The programme specifies provided helmets, ropes and gloves as well as safety instructions. The second part of the day involves quad biking, with instruction in handling and safety. These activities carry different risks; confirm the actual age, medical and technical participation conditions before joining.

[Monteverde](/costa-rica/place/monteverde-santa-elena/) introduces an entirely different natural setting. The day 8 road journey passes the Viento Fresco waterfall area, followed by bungee jumping and a Superman-style zipline ride. Weight, age, health and weather restrictions are set by the individual operator. Admission cannot be promised to every traveller in advance.

**The key question is whether every participant is ready for the active sections, not simply whether they have enough days.** If one person wants to raft and go canyoning while another prefers wildlife observation, discuss participation and activity substitutions beforehand. Optional activities are listed as a separate expense category on this tour.

## The Pacific: fishing, diving and a rest day

After the mountain forests, the group moves to the Pacific Ocean. Day 9 has no compulsory excursions. Day 10 includes **offshore sport fishing near Flamingo**: a full day on the water, not a quick beach stop. Catches depend on season, weather and marine conditions. Mentioning marlin, tuna or mahi-mahi among local species does not guarantee a catch.

Day 11 is dedicated to **diving around the [Catalina Islands](/costa-rica/place/catalina-islands/)**. The programme presents this as an option for more experienced divers. Strong currents are possible in some areas, and certain dive sites have stated depths of 12–35 m. Before booking, compare the particular dive conditions with your experience and qualifications, and confirm the number of dives, equipment and weather. Do not assume certification or equipment hire is included without specific confirmation.

Surface intervals before flying are important. Divers Alert Network recommends at least 12 hours after one no-decompression dive and at least 18 hours after repetitive or multi-day no-decompression dives; more demanding profiles require individual assessment and a larger margin. There is a free day 12 between diving on day 11 and departure on day 13, but final flight and dive timing should still be checked with an instructor and dive computer.

## What is included and what remains extra

The tour includes accommodation along the route, transfers, a Russian-speaking guide, the listed excursions and meals on specified days. Meal inclusions differ by day: the rafting section may include full board, while the coast more often specifies breakfast.

**Paid separately** are optional activities, Tortuguero National Park admission, airport fees and personal expenses. Check compulsory activities against optional ones when budgeting. See the main section of this tour page for its specific cost, available arrangements and programme: the table of places, dates and services takes precedence over this general description of the travel format.

Accommodation changes from a Tortuguero lodge to a Pacuare riverside camp, hotels near Arenal and Monteverde and a coastal stay. Your luggage must suit humid forest, cooler mountain conditions and ocean days: quick-drying clothes, closed shoes, rain protection and a dry bag for belongings on the water. Confirm specialist equipment requirements for each activity separately.

## How to decide whether this trip suits you

Consider three questions. First, are you ready for Class III–IV rafting and harness-assisted waterfall descents? Second, how important are high-activity days compared with nature walks? In Costa Rica you can compare the formats through [adventure](/interests/adventure/) and [wildlife](/interests/wildlife/) tours. Third, do you have the necessary experience for ocean dives and sufficient time to finish the trip at a relaxed pace?

Ada Tours helps agree the stage sequence, activity choices and participant requirements before booking, especially when a group has mixed levels of experience. Choose based on the most difficult compulsory day rather than the easy beach ending.

## Frequently asked questions about the Extreme Costa Rica tour

### Is this tour suitable for someone without rafting experience?

The second Pacuare section includes Class IV rapids, so the tour should not automatically be considered suitable for a beginner. Participation requirements and possible alternatives must be agreed with the rafting operator before booking.

### Can I follow the itinerary without scuba diving?

Diving takes up a separate day of the Pacific section. Discuss with Ada Tours whether the dive can be omitted or replaced with relaxation; such a change is not automatically available under the programme.

### Is there time to rest between active days?

Yes. The programme includes a quiet day at the Pacuare camp, a beach day after Monteverde and a free day 12 on the Pacific coast. The early transfers and river sections are nevertheless demanding.

### Are all entrance tickets and activities included?

No. Tortuguero National Park admission, for example, is explicitly excluded, along with optional activities. For anything unclear, check the specific itinerary and the selected tour's terms.

### When should I schedule a flight after diving?

Timing depends on the dives actually made, their depth and frequency and the diver's condition. A safe interval must separate the last dive from the flight, according to the diving professional's recommendations and current medical guidance. A free calendar day is not a substitute for checking exact times.

## Fishing in Costa Rica: 7 days near Flamingo with Pacific Ocean trips

This [Costa Rica fishing tour](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-fishing/) lasts **7 days and 6 nights**. After arriving in [San José](/costa-rica/place/san-jose/), travellers transfer to the [Pacific coast](/costa-rica/place/pacific-coast/), near [Flamingo](/costa-rica/place/flamingo/). The principal purpose is offshore sport fishing rather than a general sightseeing tour of the country.

According to the programme, the road journey from San José to the coast takes approximately four hours. Days 3–6 focus on fishing and staying in the coastal area, followed by a return transfer to the international airport. This allows several consecutive days for outings on the water rather than a single short boat trip.

## Two fishing areas: open ocean and island waters

Near Flamingo, both deep offshore Pacific fishing grounds and more coastal locations are relatively accessible. The choice depends on fishing goals, the weather and the capabilities of the particular vessel.

| Area | Main target species |
|---|---|
| Open ocean | Sailfish, marlin, mahi-mahi, tuna |
| Near the islands | Wahoo, mackerel, snappers and roosterfish |

The programme describes deep-sea fishing west of the harbour and areas near the Catalina Islands. Sailfish, different species of marlin, mahi-mahi and tuna are possible catches, not guaranteed trophies. The captain selects the precise grounds based on sea conditions and seasonal fish movement.

Inshore areas appeal to travellers who prefer shorter runs on the water or want to target different species. Even near the coast, however, calm seas cannot be guaranteed: wind and waves still affect conditions.

## How the fishing days are arranged

The first day is for arrival and accommodation in the capital. After breakfast on the second day, the group transfers to the coast. **Days 3 through 6** are mainly devoted to fishing near Flamingo. Day seven is the return airport transfer.

It is important to distinguish *days spent in the fishing area* from the precise number and duration of paid boat outings. When booking, confirm the vessel schedule, length of each trip, passenger numbers, equipment and cancellation arrangements in bad weather. The word "fishing" alone is no substitute for these commercial details.

It also helps to choose your priority in advance: targeting large pelagic fish, more varied inshore fishing, or a combination of the two. This makes it easier to agree the boat type, distance offshore and physical demands. To compare other fishing formats, see the [fishing tours catalogue](/interests/fishing/).

## Seasonality and expectations for the catch

Fishing conditions on Costa Rica's Pacific coast change with the seasons. The likelihood of encountering sailfish, marlin or mahi-mahi varies through the year. Fish migrations, water temperature, wind and accessibility of offshore grounds also differ from year to year.

When choosing dates, therefore, start with **the species you most want to catch and the fishing area**, then ask the captain for current local information. Nobody can promise a marlin catch, a tuna of a particular weight or a certain number of fish in one day. Bad weather can prevent the boat from sailing even in a well-chosen season.

## Licences, fishing rules and responsibilities

Sport fishing in Costa Rica is regulated by INCOPESCA. Participants and vessels are subject to separate permits and documentation requirements. Before departure, clarify **which permit the individual participant needs**, who will arrange it and whether the applicable fee is included in the agreed package.

Some fish species are subject to retention restrictions, and catch-and-release practices are used in sport fishing. This does not mean one rule is lawful for every species or location: check current regulations, handling of caught fish and environmental requirements against official rules and the captain's instructions.

Discuss tackle, onboard safety, seasickness remedies and arrangements for people unfamiliar with open-sea trips in advance. Follow crew instructions and use the safety equipment provided on board.

## Guides, meals and programme expenses

The price includes an English-speaking guide, transfers, hotels, specified excursions, accommodation taxes and meals on the days and to the extent stated in the programme. Optional activities, airport fees and personal expenses are listed separately.

When choosing a fishing package, additionally confirm the vessel's specifications, equipment, actual time on the water, permit costs and how the catch is handled. These cannot be inferred from the basic total trip price alone. Also distinguish accommodation ashore from staying aboard a fishing vessel: this programme uses hotels.

If fishing is meant to be only one element of a broader holiday, compare [other Costa Rica journeys](/costa-rica/tour/). This itinerary is primarily of interest because it dedicates several days in a row specifically to offshore fishing.

## Frequently asked questions about fishing near Flamingo

### How long does the trip last?

Seven days and six nights, including arrival, the coastal transfer and the return to the airport.

### Can I choose a target species in advance?

You can indicate preferred species and discuss fishing grounds, but the actual catch depends on the season and weather. Catching a particular fish cannot be guaranteed.

### Is a sport-fishing licence required?

INCOPESCA has documentation requirements for both participants and vessels. Confirm the applicable permit and application process before departure.

### Is there a Russian-speaking guide?

The tour includes an English-speaking guide. Another guiding language is not part of the confirmed tour conditions.

### Is this trip suitable for exploring Costa Rica's volcanoes?

No, this is a specialised fishing itinerary. For national parks, volcanoes and forest walks, compare [Five Wonders of Costa Rica](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-5-wonders/).

## Tortuguero and Arenal in 6 days: a Costa Rica nature tour

**This tour suits travellers who want to experience two very different natural regions of Costa Rica in one week.** Over 6 days and 5 nights, visitors discover Tortuguero's Caribbean canals, then travel to [La Fortuna and Arenal Volcano](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/).

The itinerary focuses on wildlife and landscapes. Tortuguero offers boat trips and rainforest, while the Arenal region brings hot springs, hanging bridges and walks across volcanic terrain. It does not include an extensive programme of city tours, coffee tastings or a long beach-holiday section.

Compared with the [essential five-day Costa Rica tour](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-essentials/), this itinerary includes a proper stop near Arenal instead of Doka coffee estate and La Paz waterfalls. The [10-day Costa Rica Pearls tour](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-pearls-10-days/) goes further, adding Río Celeste, Monteverde and Manuel Antonio.

## Tortuguero: waterways, forest and wildlife

Travellers leave [San José](/costa-rica/place/san-jose/) early for [Tortuguero](/costa-rica/place/tortuguero/). The road section passes through [Braulio Carrillo](/costa-rica/place/braulio-carrillo-national-park/) and banana plantations, followed by a boat transfer: this part of the Caribbean coast is more easily reached by water.

The programme includes a boat tour of the national park canals and a walk through the forest. Birds and other creatures of the humid tropics may be observed. Costa Rica's official national parks authority describes Tortuguero as a complex network of rivers, canals and swamp forests with rich biodiversity.

**Wildlife observation requires patience.** Animals may hide in vegetation, approach the water at different times or not appear along a particular section. Choose this journey for the way it lets you experience nature rather than an assumed guarantee of seeing a list of species.

The humid climate makes rain jackets, insect protection and closed shoes particularly useful. A waterproof bag for documents and a camera is advisable for boat journeys.

## Arenal: forest bridges and traces of volcanic activity

After Tortuguero, the journey continues to [La Fortuna and Arenal Volcano](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/). Day four includes a transfer and time to relax at hot springs. The following day is more active.

Travellers head to hanging bridges through tropical forest, with views of the vegetation and volcano. In the afternoon, a walk along the Los Tucanes trail is planned in the Arenal National Park area, including sections of old lava flows.

The main theme here is natural change on the volcano's slopes and the life of the forest. The tour does not include a technical summit ascent and should not be mistaken for a mountaineering expedition. Trail conditions, weather and possible park restrictions nevertheless affect comfort and access.

## How the six days are arranged

| Stage | Programme |
|---|---|
| Day 1 | Arrival in San José |
| Days 2–3 | Tortuguero, boats and forest |
| Days 4–5 | Arenal and La Fortuna |
| Day 6 | Airport or onward journey |

The final day offers **two options**: return to the international airport or continue to the next coastal holiday destination. This does not mean a beach stay is included in the six-day programme; onward travel requires separate arrangements.

This format works both as a standalone short trip and as a nature-focused part of a longer holiday. Six days involve considerable travel, leaving very few free days for extended rest.

## Included services and practical preparation

The price covers a Russian-speaking guide, transfers, hotels, excursions, meals according to the programme and the **Tortuguero–San José flight**. The detailed route also includes a transfer from Tortuguero to Arenal, so the exact sequence of all transport legs should be checked against booking terms: the overall inclusion list and individual day descriptions cover different parts of the trip.

Additional activities, airport fees, personal expenses and admission to Tortuguero National Park are excluded; the park fee is **$17 per person**. Check any changes to park rules and the current admission charge close to departure.

In a short time you will visit humid Caribbean forests and a volcanic region. Pack rainproof clothing, comfortable non-slip shoes, a light layer for cool evenings, and sun and insect protection. If particular items are needed at the hot springs, check the specifics with the operator.

## Frequently asked questions about Costa Rica for Nature Lovers

### Which natural regions fit into the six days?

The route combines Tortuguero and the Arenal area: waterways, humid forest, volcanic landscapes and hot springs.

### Are there walks or only boat trips?

Both. Tortuguero includes a forest walk, while Arenal has hanging bridges and a trail in the volcano area.

### Is beach time included?

There is no separate multi-day beach section. You may continue your journey to the coast on the final day, but that is only one possible onward option after the main programme.

### Which expenses are excluded?

These include Tortuguero park admission, optional activities, airport fees and personal spending. Consult the tour terms for the complete list.
